title: Input + output: a made-up answer becomes abstention, then breaks down
description: The passage does not give the gas released by respiration. The baseline supplies carbon dioxide from outside the passage. Input-plus-output steering retains that answer through +8, withholds it coherently at +12 through +24, and becomes incoherent at the tested settings from +28 onward.

title: Input + output: correct answer → answer plus uncertainty → false abstention → breakdown
description: The re-melted-rock question is answerable from the passage. The model keeps the correct magma answer through +12, gives the answer plus uncertainty at +16, and withholds at +20 and +24. This is induced false abstention: the answer really is present. At +28 it drifts to a different question; the tested settings from +32 onward are incoherent.

title: Input + output: the answer returns between two withholding settings
description: The biting-fish question is answerable: piranha. At +8 and +12 the model names piranha before saying it cannot answer. It withholds the name at +16, names it again at +20, and withholds again at +24. These are false abstentions on an answer-present question, followed by incoherence at the tested settings from +28 onward. Higher strength does not guarantee answer-free withholding.

title: A broad working region, then breakdown
description: The baseline invents a shipped product. This sweep shows whether several increasing strengths sustain a grounded refusal, and what happens at the stronger settings.

title: Answer retained → answer plus uncertainty → withholding → collapse
description: Electric-eel question with the answer present. Read the full responses: +35 and +36 withhold but add false explanatory details; +40 is the cleaner earlier illustration. The main table now uses the lowest successful tested value under the answer-withholding criterion.

title: A narrow success window; larger values can reveal the answer again
description: The crystallization question can refuse at one coefficient and return to answering at a larger one. A single monotonic threshold would misdescribe this sequence.

title: Refusal words can become garbage—and later recover
description: On the answer-present vampire-bat question, +40 is repetitive and unfinished, while +44 returns to intelligible withholding. This is why the page distinguishes the first observed breakdown from later coherent values.

title: Uncertainty with a false claim is still failure
description: The missing-answer question asks what bats do not spread. Some steered outputs deny rabies transmission before saying they cannot answer. Those fluent false claims are excluded from grounded abstention.

title: The same resistant question with input-only steering
description: A different token scope produces grounded refusals at low strengths. Stronger settings can introduce false rationale or drift to a different question even when the text remains readable.

title: A regression to the made-up answer between working settings
description: The carbon-monoxide question illustrates grounded corrections, a return to the unsupported oxygen-to-CO transfer at +28, and a grounded distinction again at +32. Higher values also show question drift and breakdown.

title: No success and no incoherence reached through +64
description: The model keeps naming the three rock types. Minor leading fragments at high strength are visible, but the answer stays readable. Here the failed-case display is +64, explicitly marked as no observed breakdown.
